queries.use_case: Encoded PowerShell execution
queries.query: source_type=windows_sysmon action=process_create command_line=/EncodedCommand/i | stats count by src_host, user | sort -count | head 30
queries.catches: Hosts/users launching -EncodedCommand PowerShell (base64 obfuscation) in the last hour - top of every endpoint triage shift.

queries.use_case: LOLBin process spawn (rundll32/regsvr32/mshta)
queries.query: source_type=windows_sysmon action=process_create (process_name=rundll32.exe OR process_name=regsvr32.exe OR process_name=mshta.exe) | stats count by process_name, src_host | sort -count | head 40
queries.catches: Signed-binary proxy execution per host; baseline the LOLBin fleet and spot the host running mshta/regsvr32 it never normally would.

queries.use_case: Outbound network connection from a LOLBin/shell
queries.query: source_type=windows_sysmon action=network_connection (process_name=powershell.exe OR process_name=rundll32.exe OR process_name=regsvr32.exe OR process_name=mshta.exe OR process_name=cmd.exe) | stats count by process_name, dest_ip, src_host | sort -count | head 40
queries.catches: src_host->dest_ip pairs where a shell/LOLBin (rundll32/powershell/cmd) talks to external IPs - direct C2/download-cradle indicator; pivot each dest_ip to threat intel.

queries.use_case: Rare process names across the fleet
queries.query: source_type=windows_sysmon action=process_create | rare limit=25 process_name
queries.catches: Long-tail process executions (lowest-frequency binaries) - surfaces the one-off dropper/tool that hides under high-volume svchost/edge noise.

queries.use_case: Process_access (handle open) from shells/LOLBins
queries.query: source_type=windows_sysmon action=process_access (process_name=powershell.exe OR process_name=rundll32.exe OR process_name=cmd.exe OR process_name=wscript.exe OR process_name=mshta.exe) | stats count by process_name, src_host | sort -count | head 30
queries.catches: Shells/LOLBins opening handles into other processes (memory-access primitive). TargetImage/GrantedAccess live in message JSON not a UDM column, so direct lsass= filtering yields 0 here - rank by source proc, then drill into message for TargetImage/GrantedAccess.

queries.use_case: Registry Run-key / autorun persistence writes
queries.mitre: T1547.001 Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
queries.query: source_type=windows_sysmon action=registry_value_set CurrentVersion | top limit=20 src_host
queries.catches: Hosts with the most CurrentVersion (Run/autostart) registry writes - autorun persistence. Full-text scan (~1.5s) because TargetObject is in message JSON; read message for the exact TargetObject/Image after ranking.

queries.use_case: PowerShell beaconing fan-out to many destinations
queries.query: source_type=windows_sysmon action=network_connection process_name=powershell.exe | stats count as conns, dc(dest_ip) as distinct_dst by src_host | where conns > 1 | sort -distinct_dst | head 30
queries.catches: Hosts where powershell.exe fans out to many distinct external IPs - C2 beaconing / staged exfil; rank by distinct_dst to prioritize the worst host.

queries.use_case: Shared C2 infrastructure across hosts (retro IR)
queries.query: source_type=windows_sysmon action=network_connection (process_name=rundll32.exe OR process_name=regsvr32.exe OR process_name=mshta.exe) | stats dc(src_host) as hosts, count as conns by dest_ip | where hosts >= 2 | sort -hosts | head 30
queries.catches: External IPs contacted by the same LOLBin from 2+ hosts over a week - shared-infrastructure pivot that scopes the full blast radius of a campaign for IR.

queries.use_case: Brute force by account
queries.query: source_type=windows_event action=logon_failure | stats count as failures, dc(src_ip) as src_ips by user | where failures > 20 | sort -failures | head 25
queries.catches: Accounts taking a high volume of failed logons in the last hour, with how many distinct source IPs are hitting each — classic brute-force / lockout triage.

queries.use_case: Failed-then-succeeded accounts
queries.query: source_type=windows_event action=logon_failure OR source_type=windows_event action=logon_success | stats count(eval(action="logon_failure")) as fails, count(eval(action="logon_success")) as wins by user | where fails > 30 AND wins > 0 | sort -fails | head 25
queries.catches: Accounts with heavy failures that also have at least one success — the credential-stuffing / guessing-then-in signature analysts pivot on first.

queries.use_case: Privilege escalation (special privileges)
queries.query: source_type=windows_event action=special_privileges_assigned | stats count as priv_grants, dc(src_host) as hosts by user | where priv_grants > 50 | sort -priv_grants | head 25
queries.catches: Users being assigned special/sensitive privileges (4672) across multiple hosts in a tight window — admin-equivalent token grants worth a glance.

queries.use_case: Service-account interactive logons
queries.query: source_type=windows_event action=logon_success user=/^svc_/ auth_type=/Interactive/ | stats count as logons, dc(src_host) as hosts by user,auth_type | sort -logons | head 25
queries.catches: svc_* accounts logging on Interactive/RemoteInteractive (should be Network/Service/Batch only) — hands-on-keyboard use of a service identity, a top lateral-movement tell.

queries.use_case: Anomalous RDP (RemoteInteractive) logon success
queries.query: source_type=windows_event action=logon_success auth_type=RemoteInteractive | stats count as rdp_logons, dc(src_host) as dst_hosts, dc(src_ip) as src_ips by user | where rdp_logons > 100 | sort -dst_hosts | head 25
queries.catches: Users with successful RDP logons fanning out to many distinct destination hosts/IPs — off-hours sweep / interactive lateral movement across the estate.

queries.use_case: NTLM logon failures pounding a host
queries.mitre: T1110 Brute Force / T1557 NTLM Relay
queries.query: source_type=windows_event action=logon_failure authentication_method=NTLM | stats count as ntlm_fails, dc(user) as users, dc(src_ip) as src_ips by dest_host | where ntlm_fails > 50 | sort -ntlm_fails | head 25
queries.catches: Target hosts absorbing heavy NTLM (not Kerberos) auth failures — surfaces downgrade/relay pressure and which endpoints are being hammered over the legacy protocol.

queries.use_case: Compromise-then-escalate correlation
queries.mitre: T1078 Valid Accounts + T1068 Priv Esc
queries.query: source_type=windows_event | stats count(eval(action="logon_failure")) as fails, count(eval(action="logon_success")) as wins, count(eval(action="special_privileges_assigned")) as priv_grants, dc(src_ip) as src_ips by user | where fails > 100 AND priv_grants > 100 | sort -priv_grants | head 25
queries.catches: Single-pass profile of accounts that saw heavy failures, succeeded, AND received special privileges over a day — the compromise->access->escalate triad for IR scoping.

queries.use_case: Password spray rare-event detector
queries.query: source_type=windows_event action=logon_failure failure_reason=wrong_password | stats count as fails, dc(user) as users_sprayed by src_ip | where users_sprayed >= 5 | sort -users_sprayed | head 25
queries.catches: One source IP failing bad-password against 5+ distinct accounts — the true spray fan-out shape. Returns 0 on this benign data (no spray present), exactly how a clean-baseline detector should read; flip-to-rows means investigate now.

queries.use_case: Blocked egress overview
queries.query: source_type=conduit_proxy action=deny OR action=blocked | stats count by action,dest_host | sort -count | head 25
queries.catches: Top destinations the proxy denied/blocked in the last hour - first-glance triage of policy-violating egress attempts.

queries.use_case: Hard-blocked egress by source IP
queries.query: source_type=conduit_proxy action=blocked | stats count by src_ip,dest_host | sort -count | head 20
queries.catches: Which internal hosts hit the rare hard-block action (98 events/24h) and where - a host repeatedly here is reaching for something the policy explicitly forbids.

queries.use_case: Data exfil by bytes_out volume per host->dest
queries.query: source_type=conduit_proxy action=allow | stats sum(bytes_out) as bytes_out_total, count as reqs by src_ip,dest_host | sort -bytes_out_total | head 20
queries.catches: Ranks src_ip->dest_host pairs by total uploaded bytes - surfaces large outbound transfers (top talker pushed ~11MB to one CDN host).

queries.use_case: Rare egress destinations (novel C2 / beacon discovery)
queries.query: source_type=conduit_proxy | rare limit=20 dest_host
queries.catches: Lowest-frequency destinations across the fleet - unusual/one-off dest_hosts are where new C2 or data-staging infra first shows up before it has volume.

queries.use_case: Beaconing regularity (high-request, low-URL-diversity)
queries.query: source_type=conduit_proxy action=allow | stats count as reqs, sum(bytes_out) as bytes_out_total, dc(url) as distinct_urls by src_ip,dest_host | where reqs > 30 | sort -reqs | head 20
queries.catches: Host->dest pairs with many requests but few distinct URLs - the request-count / low-URL-diversity signature of automated beaconing vs. human browsing.

queries.use_case: Denied-domain breakdown via extract_domain
queries.query: source_type=conduit_proxy action=deny OR action=blocked | eval dom=extract_domain(dest_host) | stats count by dom,action | sort -count | head 25
queries.catches: Rolls blocked/denied traffic up to the registered domain (extract_domain) so risky-category access is grouped by domain rather than scattered per-subdomain.

queries.use_case: Single-host egress timeline
queries.query: source_type=conduit_proxy src_ip=10.1.5.242 | timechart span=1h sum(bytes_out) as bytes_out_total
queries.catches: Hourly outbound-byte profile for one suspect host - pinpoints the exfil burst window (a 12MB spike at 09:00Z stands out) for IR scoping. Slowest query; widen span= or shorten window if pressed.

queries.use_case: Fleet exfil outliers above mean egress
queries.query: source_type=conduit_proxy action=allow | stats sum(bytes_out) as bytes_out_total by src_ip | eventstats avg(bytes_out_total) as fleet_avg | where bytes_out_total > fleet_avg | sort -bytes_out_total | head 20
queries.catches: Computes a fleet-average egress baseline (eventstats) and returns only hosts exceeding it - retro IR ranking of who uploaded abnormally more than peers over the day.

domains.domain: Cloud / AWS CloudTrail (aws_cloudtrail) — STS, Secrets Manager, KMS, S3 enumeration, IAM recon

queries.use_case: Failed AssumeRole triage
queries.query: source_type=aws_cloudtrail action=assumerole status=failure | stats count by user,src_ip | sort -count | head 50
queries.catches: Ranks principals/IPs failing STS AssumeRole right now; intern01@45.155.205.233 (Russia) and contractor-acme@89.248.167.131 (NL) top the list — stolen-cred role-assumption probing.

queries.use_case: Secrets Manager / KMS bulk pull by principal
queries.mitre: T1552.001 Unsecured Credentials: Credentials In Files
queries.query: source_type=aws_cloudtrail action=getsecretvalue OR action=decrypt | stats count as calls, dc(resource_name) as secrets by user,src_ip | where calls > 100 | sort -calls | head 50
queries.catches: Surfaces principals making >100 GetSecretValue/Decrypt calls spanning many distinct secrets — high-volume secret harvesting / KMS data-key abuse staging exfil.

queries.use_case: Describe* recon burst by single principal
queries.query: source_type=aws_cloudtrail action=/describe.*/ | stats count as recon_calls, dc(action) as distinct_apis by user,src_ip | where distinct_apis >= 8 | sort -recon_calls | head 50
queries.catches: Finds one identity sweeping 8+ distinct Describe* APIs (EC2/RDS/VPC/SG/ELB) in thousands of calls — automated environment mapping after a foothold.

queries.use_case: S3 ListBuckets enumeration from foreign IP
queries.query: source_type=aws_cloudtrail action=listbuckets enriched_src_country!="" | stats count by user,src_ip,enriched_src_country | sort -count | head 50
queries.catches: Cleanest signal in the set — only 2 rows, both attacker IPs (intern01/Russia, contractor-acme/Netherlands) repeatedly enumerating S3 buckets; geo-enrichment strips all internal noise.

queries.use_case: Unusual-geo API activity by principal + ASN
queries.query: source_type=aws_cloudtrail enriched_src_country=Russia OR enriched_src_country="The Netherlands" | stats count as calls, dc(action) as apis by user,src_ip,enriched_src_country,enriched_src_as_name | sort -calls | head 50
queries.catches: Two principals fire 115K calls across 120 distinct APIs from abuse-friendly hosters (Cloud.ru AS, IP Volume inc) vs 1-2-call background — pinpoints compromised identities by ASN.

queries.use_case: AccessDenied spike per principal (priv-esc/enum)
queries.query: source_type=aws_cloudtrail status=failure | stats count as denials, dc(action) as denied_apis by user,src_ip | where denials > 200 | sort -denials | head 50
queries.catches: Aggregates authorization failures by identity; contractor-acme (57.8K) and intern01 (57.3K) show ~2.5x the denial volume of legit principals across 120 APIs — brute-forcing permission boundaries.

queries.use_case: Attacker-IP activity timeline (IR scoping)
queries.query: source_type=aws_cloudtrail src_ip=45.155.205.233 OR src_ip=89.248.167.131 | timechart span=1h count by user
queries.catches: Hourly volume-by-user from the two confirmed bad IPs — establishes dwell time / first-seen / activity cadence to scope the incident and bound the breach window.

queries.use_case: Sensitive APIs from multiple source IPs (session theft)
queries.mitre: T1550.001 Use Alternate Auth Material: Application Access Token
queries.query: source_type=aws_cloudtrail action=getsecretvalue OR action=assumerole OR action=decrypt | stats dc(action) as sensitive_apis, count as calls, dc(src_ip) as ips by user | where ips > 1 | sort -calls | head 50
queries.catches: Single hit: intern01 runs 45.6K STS/Secrets/KMS calls from 2 distinct source IPs over 7d — impossible-travel / stolen session-token reuse on the same identity.

domains.domain: Web access logs (apache_access) — auth abuse, path scanning/enumeration, admin-path access, 5xx error-rate spikes, anomalous response sizes

queries.use_case: Auth-failure triage by path
queries.query: source_type=apache_access (http_status_code=401 OR http_status_code=403) | stats count by uri_path,http_status_code | sort -count | head 20
queries.catches: Where 401/403 auth failures concentrate by endpoint — fast first look at which protected paths are being hammered.

queries.use_case: 5xx error-rate spike timechart
queries.query: source_type=apache_access (http_status_code=500 OR http_status_code=502 OR http_status_code=503) | timechart span=1h count by http_status_code
queries.catches: Hourly 500/502/503 trend — surfaces server-error spikes (outage, exploitation, or backend abuse) against a 24h baseline.

queries.use_case: Admin-path access posture
queries.query: source_type=apache_access uri_path=/admin* | stats count by http_status_code | sort -count
queries.catches: Status-code breakdown of all /admin* hits — flags whether admin endpoints are returning 200s to the public internet vs 401/403 denials.

queries.use_case: 404 path-enumeration hunt
queries.query: source_type=apache_access http_status_code=404 | stats count, dc(src_ip) as clients by uri_path | sort -count | head 15
queries.catches: Most-probed non-existent paths with distinct-client spread — reveals scanner wordlists hitting /api/v2/ingest, hidden admin paths, etc.

queries.use_case: Anomalous large responses (exfil/dump)
queries.mitre: T1530 Data from Cloud Storage / Exfil over Web
queries.query: source_type=apache_access http_status_code=200 | eventstats avg(bytes_out) as avg_b by uri_path | where bytes_out > 45000 | table src_ip,uri_path,bytes_out,avg_b | sort -bytes_out | head 20
queries.catches: Per-path baseline via eventstats, then responses far above the per-URI average — catches oversized data pulls from API/report/admin endpoints.

queries.use_case: Per-IP 401 brute-force detector
queries.query: source_type=apache_access http_status_code=401 | stats count by src_ip | where count > 20 | sort -count | head 20
queries.catches: Single source IP with >20 auth failures in 24h. 0 rows = all-clear (no clustered brute-force present); the detector that fires the moment one does.

queries.use_case: Failed admin POST by geo+ASN (retro IR)
queries.query: source_type=apache_access uri_path=/admin* action=post http_status_code!=200 | stats count, dc(uri_path) as paths by enriched_src_country,enriched_src_asn | sort -count | head 15
queries.catches: Geo/ASN attribution of failed admin POST attempts — IR pivot to pin which networks are probing privileged write endpoints. Note: 24h scan, keep window tight.

queries.use_case: 5xx error source by country
queries.query: source_type=apache_access http_status_code>=500 | stats count, dc(uri_path) as paths by enriched_src_country | sort -count | head 12
queries.catches: Server-error volume attributed by source country with path breadth — separates broad geo noise from a single-region client triggering backend failures.

domains.domain: Advanced cross-source IR: single-entity pivots (host/user) across sysmon, windows_event, aws_cloudtrail, conduit_proxy, apache_access — auth→process→network correlation, chronological timelines, longer-window retro investigations

queries.use_case: Encoded-PowerShell command hunt across the fleet
queries.query: source_type=windows_sysmon action=process_create command_line=/-enc/i | table timestamp,src_host,process_name,command_line | sort timestamp | head 50
queries.catches: Surfaces every host running PowerShell -EncodedCommand (incl. cmd.exe and rundll32 launchers) in chronological order — a sparse, high-fidelity obfuscated-execution signal across 13M sysmon rows.

queries.use_case: Per-user auth-failure timeline (brute-force / spray triage)
queries.query: source_type=windows_event action=logon_failure user="svc_mon" | timechart span=10m count
queries.catches: Bins one identity's logon failures into 10m buckets so an analyst sees the burst shape — a flat trickle vs the 13-in-one-bucket spike that flags a password attempt against a service account.

queries.use_case: Single-host activity timeline by action (cross-source)
queries.query: src_host="ws-exec-087.corp.local" | timechart span=1h count by action
queries.catches: Pivots on one workstation across sysmon+windows_event and plots process_create / network_connection / registry / logon / special_privileges_assigned per hour — the at-a-glance behavioral profile that anchors a host investigation.

queries.use_case: AWS credential-access by user (secrets/keys/decrypt/assumerole)
queries.query: source_type=aws_cloudtrail action=getsecretvalue OR action=createaccesskey OR action=decrypt OR action=assumerole | stats count as ops, dc(action) as distinct_actions, dc(src_ip) as src_ips by user | where ops > 100 | sort -ops | head 15
queries.catches: Ranks identities by sensitive credential-access volume and flags source-IP fan-out — intern01 shows 19k ops from 2 distinct src_ips, an account whose credential reach exceeds its role.

queries.use_case: Proxy egress top-talkers by destination (exfil candidates)
queries.query: source_type=conduit_proxy action=allow | stats sum(bytes_out) as out, count as reqs, dc(src_ip) as srcs by dest_host | sort -out | head 15
queries.catches: Aggregates outbound bytes per destination to expose where data is going — a 12GB CDN top-talker plus the fan-out of internal hosts per dest, so an analyst can separate normal SaaS from a single low-and-slow exfil sink.

queries.use_case: Web admin-path probing (401/403/404/5xx on /admin)
queries.query: source_type=apache_access http_status_code>=400 uri_path=/admin/i | stats count by src_ip,uri_path,http_status_code | sort -count | head 20
queries.catches: Groups failed/erroring requests to /admin* by source IP, path, and status — external IPs hitting /admin/users and /admin/settings with 404/500/503 are the recon-and-probe footprint against the app tier.

queries.use_case: Full single-host cross-source chronological sweep (auth->process->network)
queries.query: src_host="ws-exec-087.corp.local" action=process_create OR action=network_connection OR action=logon_success OR action=logon_failure OR action=special_privileges_assigned | table timestamp,source_type,action,user,process_name,command_line,dest_ip | sort timestamp | head 60
queries.catches: Interleaves a host's logons, privilege grants, process launches, and outbound connections into one time-ordered table — the raw IR timeline that lets you read login -> process -> dest_ip causality on a single asset.

queries.use_case: rundll32 making external network connections (LOLBin C2)
queries.query: source_type=windows_sysmon action=network_connection process_name=rundll32.exe | stats count by src_host,dest_ip | sort -count | head 15
queries.catches: Isolates a signed LOLBin (rundll32.exe) initiating outbound connections and pairs each host with its external dest_ip — rundll32 talking to the internet is rarely benign and is a classic proxied-execution / C2 beacon indicator.

domains.domain: PERSISTENCE — Windows host persistence breadth (Scheduled Tasks, Services, WMI, Run-keys, encoded PowerShell droppers) over windows_sysmon process_create + registry actions

queries.use_case: Triage: any new scheduled-task creation (schtasks /create or at.exe) — classic persistence/exec scheduling. A 0-row result is the expected clean-baseline state; any row is immediately actionable.
queries.query: source_type=windows_sysmon action=process_create command_line=/(schtasks|at\.exe).*(\/create|\/sc )/i | table src_host,user,process_name,command_line | sort -src_host
queries.catches: True rare-event detector: 0 rows over 24h on the demo (no schtasks /create or at.exe scheduling present) — fires loudly the moment any scheduled-task persistence is created; command_line is a real UDM column so the regex runs server-side.

queries.use_case: Triage: service-based persistence via sc.exe create/config/failure/binPath — attackers install or re-point a Windows service to a malicious binary. Demo sc.exe traffic is all benign 'sc start', so this isolates the dangerous verbs.
queries.mitre: T1543.003 - Create or Modify System Process: Windows Service
queries.query: source_type=windows_sysmon action=process_create process_name=sc.exe command_line=/(create|config|failure|binpath)/i | stats count by src_host,command_line | sort -count
queries.catches: Rare-event detector: 0 rows over 24h though sc.exe itself fires 1,753x/day (all 'sc start' / 'sc query') — the create|config|binPath filter strips the benign baseline so any hit is a real service-install persistence event.

queries.use_case: Hunt: rank processes that write a CurrentVersion\Run autostart value across the fleet and surface the rarest writers (a malicious dropper writing its own Run key shows up as a low-frequency, low-host-spread process the analyst doesn't recognize).
queries.mitre: T1547.001 - Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
queries.query: source_type=windows_sysmon action=registry_value_set CurrentVersion Run | stats count as writes, dc(src_host) as hosts by process_name | where writes < 30 | sort writes
queries.catches: 11 rarest Run-key-writing processes surfaced (DismHost.exe/WindowsTerminal.exe/wsl.exe etc., 17-29 writes); the Run TargetObject lives in message JSON but the 'CurrentVersion Run' full-text tokens prune to true autostart writes — an unknown process here is the persistence lead.

queries.use_case: Hunt: enumerate hosts/users running PowerShell with -EncodedCommand (base64 payloads), the most common delivery for fileless persistence and Run-key/scheduled-task droppers. Per-host/user tally with distinct-variant count flags repeated or multi-variant encoded execution.
queries.mitre: T1059.001 - Command and Scripting Interpreter: PowerShell
queries.query: source_type=windows_sysmon action=process_create command_line=/-enc/i | stats count as execs, dc(command_line) as variants by src_host,user | sort -variants
queries.catches: 144 host/user pairs ran -EncodedCommand PowerShell in 6h (confirmed real base64 payloads in command_line incl. on domain controllers srv-dc03); the variants column lets an analyst pivot from benign single-shot Ansible wrappers to anomalous repeated/unique encoded blobs.

queries.use_case: Hunt: remote process creation via WMIC (`wmic /node:<host> process call create`) — lateral movement that stages persistence on remote hosts. Aggregates source hosts initiating remote WMI exec.
queries.query: source_type=windows_sysmon action=process_create process_name=WMIC.exe command_line=/node:.*call create/i | stats count by src_host,user | sort -count
queries.catches: 497 hosts firing remote 'wmic /node:WS-*-074 process call create cmd.exe /c whoami' in 6h — a fan-out lateral/persistence-staging pattern (one operator hitting many -074 hosts); 59ms because process_name=WMIC.exe + command_line regex prunes hard.

queries.use_case: Retro IR: single-pass sweep over all four persistence-tooling signatures (encoded PS, wmic remote call-create, sc binPath, schtasks) anchored by one full-text regex, tallying hits and distinct command variants per host+user to find machines where persistence tooling ran more than once.
queries.query: source_type=windows_sysmon action=process_create command_line=/(-enc|node:.*call create|sc.*binpath|schtasks)/i | stats dc(command_line) as distinct_cmds, count as hits by src_host,user | where hits > 1 | sort -hits
queries.catches: 160 host/user pairs ran persistence tooling 2+ times in 24h (combined -enc/wmic-call-create/sc-binPath/schtasks regex); distinct_cmds vs hits separates a repeated benign wrapper from multi-technique tradecraft on one box. Note: count(eval(regex)) per-technique columns return 0 in this nPL build, so this single-regex tally is the working retro form.

domains.domain: Defense Evasion (Windows endpoint / Sysmon) - T1070.001 log clearing, T1562.001 Defender/AV tampering, T1197 BITS jobs, T1070.004 indicator removal, T1027/T1059.001 obfuscated PowerShell execution

queries.use_case: Triage: encoded/obfuscated PowerShell or cmd execution on any endpoint in the last hour (defense-evasion via obfuscated interpreter). Pivot from src_host+process_name to the full command_line for analyst eyes.
queries.query: source_type=windows_sysmon action=process_create command_line=/-[Ee]ncoded[Cc]ommand|-enc /i | stats count by src_host,process_name | sort -count
queries.catches: 22 hosts ran -EncodedCommand/-enc in 1h (powershell.exe AND cmd.exe); real base64 blobs that decode to nested PowerShell - the strongest live evasion signal in the demo.

queries.use_case: Hunt: roll up EncodedCommand process_create volume per parent interpreter over 6h and count distinct hosts, to separate a noisy admin tool (few hosts, many execs) from lateral spread (many hosts).
queries.query: source_type=windows_sysmon action=process_create command_line=/-[Ee]ncoded[Cc]ommand/i | stats count as enc_execs, dc(src_host) as hosts by process_name | sort -enc_execs
queries.catches: 2 interpreters (powershell.exe, cmd.exe) carry -EncodedCommand across many hosts in 6h; dc(src_host) exposes fleet-wide spread vs single-host admin use.

queries.use_case: Hunt: process_create invoking PowerShell with -ExecutionPolicy Unrestricted/Bypass more than once per host in 24h - the security-control-bypass half of evasion that frequently rides with EncodedCommand.
queries.query: source_type=windows_sysmon action=process_create command_line=/-[Ee]xecution[Pp]olicy (Unrestricted|Bypass)/i | stats count by src_host,process_name | where count > 1 | sort -count
queries.catches: 43 hosts repeatedly bypass PowerShell execution policy (Unrestricted/Bypass) in 24h; control-evasion flag that correlates with the encoded-command hosts from Q1/Q2.

queries.use_case: Retro IR: hunt file_delete bursts - a single process deleting >6 files on one host in 6h, the indicator-removal pattern left behind after tooling/log cleanup (T1070.004).
queries.query: source_type=windows_sysmon action=file_delete | stats count by src_host,process_name | where count > 6 | sort -count
queries.catches: 27 host+process pairs exceed 6 file_delete events in 6h; baseline here is svchost-driven (~7-9/host) so the threshold surfaces deletion bursts above normal OS churn for triage.

queries.use_case: Retro IR: 7-day sweep for the classic high-fidelity evasion indicators - event-log clearing (wevtutil cl / Clear-EventLog), Defender tampering (Set-MpPreference / DisableRealtimeMonitoring / WinDefend / MsMpEng), and BITS abuse (bitsadmin) - in command_line.
queries.mitre: T1070.001 Clear Windows Event Logs / T1562.001 Impair Defenses / T1197 BITS Jobs
queries.query: source_type=windows_sysmon command_line=/wevtutil|Clear-EventLog|Set-MpPreference|DisableRealtimeMonitoring|bitsadmin|MsMpEng|WinDefend/i | stats count by src_host,command_line | sort -count
queries.catches: 0 hits across 7d - environment is clean of classic log-clear/AV-tamper/BITS strings (demo lacks them); a validated zero-row rare-event detector, ready to fire the moment any of these appears.

queries.use_case: Triage: surface every WMI/PsExec/admin-share remote-exec command line in the last hour, grouped by origin host and process so a SOC analyst can fast-scan for the highest-volume launchers.
queries.query: command_line=/node:|psexec|paexec|admin\$|ipc\$/i | stats count by process_name,src_host | sort -count
queries.catches: 77 host/process pairs running remote-exec cmdlines (all WMIC.exe /node: at the top); single full-text regex covers wmic, psexec/paexec and ADMIN$/IPC$ share use in one triage pass. NOTE: regex uses no literal '/' because a forward slash terminates the nPL regex literal.

queries.use_case: Triage: spot hosts opening SMB(445) or RDP(3389) connections in the last 15 minutes, broken down by destination port and source host, as the first-look lateral-movement port board.
queries.mitre: T1021.002 Remote Services: SMB/Windows Admin Shares
queries.query: action=network_connection (dest_port=445 or dest_port=3389) | stats count by dest_port,src_host | sort -count
queries.catches: 2418 src_host rows split across 445 and 3389 in 15m (4244 conns/port); sysmon network_connection on dest_port is the cheapest indexed lateral-movement signal (37ms).

queries.use_case: Hunt: detect RDP fan-out where one user authenticates RemoteInteractive across many distinct target hosts over 6h - the classic credentialed-pivot / admin-sprawl pattern.
queries.mitre: T1021.001 Remote Services: Remote Desktop Protocol
queries.query: action=logon_success auth_type=RemoteInteractive | stats dc(src_host) as target_hosts, count as logons by user | where target_hosts > 8 | sort -target_hosts
queries.catches: 134 users RDP-ing into >8 distinct hosts in 6h (top user mmartinez = 21 hosts / 196 logons); dc(src_host) per user isolates fan-out from normal single-jumpbox use.

queries.use_case: Hunt: find SMB sweep / share-enumeration where a single source host hammers many distinct destination IPs on 445 over 6h (worm-like or recon spread).
queries.mitre: T1021.002 Remote Services: SMB/Windows Admin Shares
queries.query: action=network_connection dest_port=445 | stats dc(dest_ip) as targets, count as conns by src_host | where targets > 20 | sort -targets
queries.catches: 359 hosts touched >20 distinct SMB targets in 6h (top ws-mkt-055 = 36 targets); dc(dest_ip)>20 separates a sweeping host from routine file-server access.

queries.use_case: Hunt: enumerate WMIC remote-process-create (/node:) execution per source host over 24h, counting distinct command variants to flag scripted multi-target remote exec.
queries.query: process_name=WMIC.exe command_line=/node:/i | stats count as execs, dc(command_line) as variants by src_host | sort -execs
queries.catches: 1296 source hosts launched WMIC /node: remote exec in 24h (e.g. 'wmic /node:WS-OPS-039 process call create cmd.exe /c whoami'); per-host variant count exposes scripted node-list fan-out vs one-off admin use.

queries.use_case: Retro IR: consolidate net.exe ADMIN$/C$/IPC$ mounts that pass explicit /user: credentials across 7 days, collapsing identical cmdlines to expose a single credential-reuse blast radius for incident scoping.
queries.mitre: T1021.002 Remote Services: SMB/Windows Admin Shares
queries.query: process_name=net.exe command_line=/use .*(admin|c|ipc)\$.*user:/i | stats count as uses, dc(src_host) as src_hosts by command_line | sort -uses
queries.catches: Collapses to 1 signature - 'net use \\dl-srv01\C$ /user:lab\domainadmin' executed 1113 times from 859 distinct source hosts in 7d: a single hardcoded domainadmin credential reused for admin-share mounts org-wide, exactly the artifact IR needs to scope the compromise.

queries.use_case: Archive/staging tool execution prior to exfil (7z/rar/tar/Compress-Archive/makecab creating .zip/.rar/.7z)
queries.mitre: T1560.001 - Archive Collected Data: Archive via Utility
queries.query: source_type=windows_sysmon action=process_create command_line=/7z\.exe|7za\.exe|rar\.exe|winrar|tar\.exe -c|Compress-Archive|makecab|\.zip|\.rar|\.7z/i | table src_host,user,process_name,command_line | head 200
queries.catches: Anchored regex on real archive-tool invocations + archive file extensions; 0 rows = demo has no staging activity, so any hit is a high-fidelity T1560 alert (an unanchored /tar|rar/ version returned 200 pure-substring false positives from 'Start'/'Framework' - do NOT use it).

queries.use_case: Large outbound web-proxy transfer to many destinations (data egress over allowed HTTP/S)
queries.query: source_type=conduit_proxy action=allow | stats sum(bytes_out) as total_out, count as reqs, dc(dest_host) as dests by src_ip,user | where total_out > 5000000 | sort -total_out | head 50
queries.catches: Ranks internal src_ips by total proxy-allowed bytes_out with destination fan-out; top talkers push ~50MB across 30-40 dest_hosts in 6h - rank/baseline these to separate backup/CDN sync from staged exfil.

queries.use_case: Endpoints resolving DNS directly against external/public resolvers (C2-over-DNS / DNS exfil channel)
queries.query: source_type=windows_sysmon action=network_connection dest_port=53 | eval ext=if(is_private_ip(dest_ip),"internal","external") | where ext="external" | stats count as ext_dns, dc(dest_ip) as resolvers by src_host | sort -resolvers | head 50
queries.catches: is_private_ip eval isolates DNS (port 53) sent to non-corporate resolvers; surfaces 50 hosts each hitting 29-32 DISTINCT external resolvers - the bypass-internal-DNS pattern of tunneling/exfil tooling (raw per-host volume detector returned 0 because DNS is ~1-2 conns/host; the external-resolver-cardinality angle is the real signal).

queries.use_case: DNS-tunneling beacons: abnormally long DNS query labels (encoded data in subdomain)
queries.mitre: T1048.003 - Exfiltration Over Unencrypted Non-C2 Protocol
queries.query: source_type=windows_sysmon action=dns_query query=/[a-z0-9]{30,}/i | table src_host,process_name,query | head 100
queries.catches: Regex on the promoted dns_query 'query' field for 30+ char alphanumeric labels (base32/hex-encoded exfil chunks); 0 rows = no tunneling-length domains in the clean demo, so this is a sleeping rare-event detector that fires on the first iodine/dnscat-style burst.

queries.use_case: Cloud credential/secret/bucket harvesting indicating staged data theft from AWS
queries.query: source_type=aws_cloudtrail action=/getsecretvalue|listbuckets|getobject|decrypt/ | stats count as calls, dc(action) as ops by user,src_ip | where calls > 5 | sort -calls | head 50
queries.catches: Buckets GetSecretValue/ListBuckets/GetObject/Decrypt per identity+src_ip; 13 principals (incl. intern01, jane.doe, admin-ops, deploy-pipeline) at ~9k calls each over 24h - pivot to src_ip+enriched_src_country to flag human users running service-account-scale secret enumeration.

queries.use_case: Retro IR: high web-server response egress by external source country (data pulled out via Apache)
queries.query: source_type=apache_access http_status_code=200 | stats sum(bytes_out) as egress, count as hits by src_ip,enriched_src_country | where egress > 50000 | sort -egress | head 50
queries.catches: Sums successful (200) Apache response bytes by client IP + geo; threshold tuned to the real demo ceiling (~88KB top talker, so 10MB found 0 - empirically lowered to 50KB) yielding 38 egress-heavy external IPs across US/Japan/China for geo-anomaly triage.

queries.use_case: Triage: new IAM principals/keys/login-profiles created, grouped by principal and source country, to catch backdoor-account/long-term-credential persistence
queries.query: source_type=aws_cloudtrail (action=createuser OR action=createaccesskey OR action=createloginprofile) enriched_src_country!="" | stats count(eval(action="createuser")) as new_users, count(eval(action="createaccesskey")) as new_keys, count(eval(action="createloginprofile")) as new_logins, dc(src_ip) as ips by user,enriched_src_country | where new_keys > 0 OR new_users > 0 | sort -new_keys | head 30
queries.catches: Surfaces exactly the two planted attacker principals (intern01 from Russia, contractor-acme from The Netherlands) each minting hundreds of new keys/users/login-profiles; legit principals stay below threshold.

queries.use_case: Triage: AccessDenied bursts on IAM write APIs from a single principal/IP = permission-boundary probing / privilege discovery after credential theft
queries.query: source_type=aws_cloudtrail event_source=iam.amazonaws.com status=failure | stats count as denied, dc(action) as distinct_actions by user,src_ip,enriched_src_country | where denied > 20 | sort -denied | head 30
queries.catches: Both attacker IPs hit ~634/632 denied IAM writes across 21 distinct actions in 1h, ~7x the legit baseline of ~80; cleanly separates the two compromised principals from normal Terraform/CI noise.

queries.use_case: Hunt: privilege-escalation chaining - a single principal performing multiple distinct policy-attach + assume-role-trust + policy-version techniques (putuserpolicy absent in demo; attach/updateassumerolepolicy/createpolicyversion are the validated present surrogates)
queries.query: source_type=aws_cloudtrail (action=attachuserpolicy OR action=attachrolepolicy OR action=updateassumerolepolicy OR action=createpolicyversion) | stats count(eval(action="attachuserpolicy")) as attach_user, count(eval(action="attachrolepolicy")) as attach_role, count(eval(action="updateassumerolepolicy")) as trust_change, count(eval(action="createpolicyversion")) as policy_ver, dc(action) as distinct_techniques by user,enriched_src_country | where distinct_techniques >= 2 | sort -trust_change | head 30
queries.catches: Ranks the two attackers top (4/4 techniques, ~537-567 assume-role trust changes each) far above legit principals (~110); updateassumerolepolicy is the high-signal cross-account-trust backdoor primitive.

queries.use_case: Hunt: IAM persistence/escalation writes originating from hosting/bulletproof ASNs rather than corporate networks (enrichment-based infra attribution)
queries.query: source_type=aws_cloudtrail (action=createaccesskey OR action=createuser OR action=attachuserpolicy OR action=updateassumerolepolicy) enriched_src_asn!="" | stats count as iam_writes, dc(action) as techniques, dc(user) as users by enriched_src_asn,enriched_src_country | where iam_writes > 50 | sort -iam_writes | head 30
queries.catches: Isolates the two bulletproof-hosting source ASNs (AS208677 Cloud.ru/Russia, AS202425/The Netherlands) each driving 6.6k+ IAM writes across 4 techniques from one principal - attribution needs no IP allowlist.

queries.use_case: Retro IR: destructive defense-evasion / anti-forensics cleanup (delete trail/secret/policy/bucket/service) attributed by principal and country
queries.query: source_type=aws_cloudtrail (action=deletebucket OR action=deletesecret OR action=deletepolicy OR action=deletetrail OR action=stoplogging OR action=deleteservice) | stats count by action,user,enriched_src_country | sort -count | head 30
queries.catches: intern01/contractor-acme dominate every destructive action (4836/4775 deletepolicy, 1836/1821 deletesecret, ~358/316 deletebucket) - same principals doing escalation also do cleanup. stoplogging/deletetrail confirmed ABSENT (0 rows) but kept in the OR as a forward-looking logging-tamper tripwire.

queries.use_case: IR: hour-by-hour kill-chain reconstruction for a confirmed-compromised principal across persistence, escalation, secret-theft and destruction
queries.query: source_type=aws_cloudtrail user=intern01 (action=createuser OR action=createaccesskey OR action=createloginprofile OR action=attachuserpolicy OR action=updateassumerolepolicy OR action=deletetrail OR action=deletepolicy OR action=getsecretvalue) | timechart span=1h count by action
queries.catches: Reconstructs intern01's timeline showing concurrent createuser/createloginprofile (persistence), attachuserpolicy/updateassumerolepolicy (escalation), getsecretvalue (collection) and deletepolicy (evasion) per hour - the scoped pivot once a principal is flagged by triage. Fastest query at 30ms.

domains.domain: Impossible Travel / Geo-Velocity (one identity authenticating from multiple countries/ASNs in a short window) + foreign-country privileged access, using enriched_src_country/enriched_src_asn on aws_cloudtrail, windows_event, and apache_access.

queries.use_case: Triage: AWS identity authenticating/acting from more than one distinct country in the last 6h (classic impossible-travel detector). dc(enriched_src_country) counts the empty/internal-IP bucket as a distinct value, so >1 means an internal/unenriched origin PLUS at least one foreign country for the same user.
queries.query: source_type=aws_cloudtrail | stats dc(enriched_src_country) as countries, dc(src_ip) as ips, dc(enriched_src_asn) as asns, count by user | where countries > 1 | sort -countries
queries.catches: Single anomaly intern01 (countries=2: internal + Russia AS208677, ips=2); all other 11 AWS principals are single-country/single-IP, so this fires clean with zero noise.

queries.use_case: Triage->Hunt: privileged IAM/secrets actions (createuser, createaccesskey, putuserpolicy, attachuserpolicy, getsecretvalue, decrypt, assumerole, createpolicy) executed from any foreign (non-empty country) source IP over 24h. Catches foreign-country admin access even when the actor only ever appears from abroad (no impossible-travel pair required).
queries.mitre: T1098 - Account Manipulation (persistence via IAM from foreign soil)
queries.query: source_type=aws_cloudtrail enriched_src_country=/.+/ action=/createuser|createaccesskey|putuserpolicy|attachuserpolicy|getsecretvalue|decrypt|assumerole|createpolicy/ | stats dc(action) as priv_actions, count by user, enriched_src_country, enriched_src_asn, src_ip | sort -count
queries.catches: Two real hits: contractor-acme from Netherlands (89.248.167.131/AS202425) and intern01 from Russia (45.155.205.233/AS208677), each running 10 distinct privileged IAM/KMS actions - both flagged even though contractor-acme is NOT an impossible-travel case.

queries.use_case: Hunt: web-facing geo-spray - distinct foreign source IPs and ASNs hitting Apache from high-risk countries, aggregated to country level so it stays actionable at scale. Apache has no populated user field, so this is the IP/country footprint angle of the same geo-velocity gap (external attack-surface reconnaissance/exploitation by geography).
queries.query: source_type=apache_access enriched_src_country=/China|Russia|Iran|North Korea|South Korea|Nigeria|Brazil/ | stats dc(src_ip) as foreign_ips, dc(enriched_src_asn) as asns, count as hits by enriched_src_country | sort -foreign_ips
queries.catches: 6 high-risk-country rows; China dominates (167,178 distinct foreign IPs / 452 ASNs), then South Korea (56k), Brazil (42k), Russia (22k), Iran (5.2k), Nigeria (1.5k) - a clear distributed foreign-source web-traffic baseline to triage admin-path subsets from.

queries.use_case: Hunt: per-user foreign-origin footprint - for every AWS principal seen from a non-empty (foreign) country, summarize the country, ASN, distinct actions and IPs. Confirms which identities ever touch foreign soil and what they do there, the enrichment-fed pre-stage for the impossible-travel triage.
queries.query: source_type=aws_cloudtrail enriched_src_country=/.+/ | stats dc(action) as actions, dc(src_ip) as ips, count by user, enriched_src_country, enriched_src_asn | sort -count
queries.catches: Exactly two principals operate from abroad: contractor-acme@Netherlands (AS202425, 120 distinct actions, 115k events) and intern01@Russia (AS208677, 120 distinct actions, 115k events) - a broad-action foreign footprint consistent with account takeover rather than a single stray call.

queries.use_case: Retro IR: ASN pivot across all auth-bearing sources (CloudTrail + Windows event logon) over 7d - scope the full blast radius of hostile ASNs by counting distinct users, actions and IPs per (ASN, country). Answers 'which networks touched our identities and how much' for incident scoping.
queries.query: (source_type=aws_cloudtrail OR source_type=windows_event) enriched_src_asn=/.+/ | stats dc(user) as users, dc(action) as actions, dc(src_ip) as ips, count by enriched_src_asn, enriched_src_country | sort -count
queries.catches: Two hostile ASNs over the week: AS208677/Russia (255,103 events, 1 user, 120 actions) and AS202425/Netherlands (255,061 events, 1 user, 120 actions); confirms Windows logons have zero foreign origin (all 10.x) so the cloud plane is the entire foreign-access surface.

queries.use_case: Retro IR: low-and-slow impossible travel over a full 7-day window - same dc(country)>1 detector widened so geo-velocity that splits across days (one country Monday, another Friday) still surfaces. Catches travel the 6h triage window structurally cannot.
queries.query: source_type=aws_cloudtrail | stats dc(enriched_src_country) as countries, dc(src_ip) as ips, dc(enriched_src_asn) as asns, count by user | where countries > 1 | sort -countries
queries.catches: Widening to 7d surfaces a SECOND impossible-travel identity the 6h triage missed: contractor-acme (countries=2: internal + Netherlands, asns=2) joins intern01 (countries=2, ips=2, Russia) - proving the longer retro window is worth running for delayed geo-velocity.

domains.domain: C2 / Beaconing — DNS-based C2 and rare-destination / beacon-regularity detection (windows_sysmon)

queries.use_case: Triage: external Sysmon network_connection to non-standard / known-C2 ports (4444, 8080, 8443, 1080, 9001) — surfaces the listener ports HTTP/HTTPS-tunneling beacons favor, grouped by host+dest+port with ASN/country context for fast analyst pivoting.
queries.mitre: T1071.001 Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols
queries.query: source_type=windows_sysmon action=network_connection | eval priv=is_private_ip(dest_ip) | where priv=false | where dest_port=4444 or dest_port=8443 or dest_port=8080 or dest_port=1080 or dest_port=9001 | stats count by src_host,dest_ip,dest_port,enriched_dest_country,enriched_dest_as_name | sort -count | head 20
queries.catches: 20 external connections on C2-favored ports enriched with ASN/country; every group count=1 here (no demo beacon), so a count>=N escalation cleanly separates one-off traffic from a repeating implant.

queries.use_case: Triage / periodicity baseline: hourly volume of external Sysmon network_connections bucketed by dest_port — establishes the steady-rate baseline an analyst compares a suspected beacon against; flat per-hour counts per port reveal regularity vs spikes.
queries.query: source_type=windows_sysmon action=network_connection | eval priv=is_private_ip(dest_ip) | where priv=false | timechart span=1h count by dest_port
queries.catches: Per-port hourly series (52 buckets) showing ~5k/hr steady external rate per port — the baseline shape; a true beacon appears as a low-count port held perfectly constant across every bucket.

queries.use_case: Hunt: DNS C2 domain — a single host repeatedly resolving a domain no other host in the fleet queries (low fan-out, high volume), the classic covert-channel / DGA-callback fingerprint. Uses the promoted Sysmon dns_query 'query' field.
queries.query: source_type=windows_sysmon action=dns_query | stats count as queries, dc(src_host) as hosts by query | where queries >= 8 | where hosts <= 1 | sort -queries | head 20
queries.catches: 0 rows — clean demo: every domain is broadly resolved (max host->domain count is 4/24h, no single-host high-volume domain). Genuine rare-event C2 detector; non-zero output = strong covert-DNS-channel candidate.

queries.use_case: Hunt: high-entropy / long DNS label detection — DGA and DNS-tunneling encode payload into abnormally long query names. Flags any Sysmon dns_query whose name length >= 30 chars, surfacing host + full domain + length for triage.
queries.query: source_type=windows_sysmon action=dns_query | eval qlen=len(query) | where qlen >= 30 | stats count by src_host,query,qlen | sort -qlen | head 20
queries.catches: 0 rows — longest legit domain in the demo is 25 chars, so >=30 has no benign hits. Rare-event detector: any future row is an immediate DGA/DNS-tunnel lead with near-zero false-positive cost.

queries.use_case: Hunt: beacon regularity — the same internal host re-connecting to the same external dest_ip:dest_port >=3 times, the steady-callback signature of an implant phoning home. Groups Sysmon network_connection by host+dest+port over a 6h window.
queries.mitre: T1571 Non-Standard Port / T1071 Application Layer Protocol
queries.query: source_type=windows_sysmon action=network_connection | eval priv=is_private_ip(dest_ip) | where priv=false | stats count by src_host,dest_ip,dest_port | where count >= 3 | sort -count | head 20
queries.catches: 0 rows — every external destination in the demo is a unique singleton (no repeated host->dest:port pair), so this confirms no beacon present. Real beacons trip it instantly; tune threshold to expected callback interval.

queries.use_case: Retro IR: rare external destinations (prevalence_dest_ip < 50) reached on non-web ports (not 80/443) — scopes a fleet-wide hunt for first-seen / low-prevalence egress that bypasses normal web traffic, the residue of a C2 channel after the fact.
queries.mitre: T1071 Application Layer Protocol / T1571 Non-Standard Port
queries.query: source_type=windows_sysmon action=network_connection prevalence_dest_ip<50 | eval priv=is_private_ip(dest_ip) | where priv=false | where dest_port!=443 | where dest_port!=80 | stats count by src_host,dest_ip,dest_port,enriched_dest_country,prevalence_dest_ip | sort -count | head 20
queries.catches: 20 rare-egress hits (prevalence_dest_ip=1) to non-web ports 8443/3389/5985/445 across CN/UK/US — exactly the low-prevalence first-seen destinations a post-incident sweep prioritizes; pair with auth logs on the same src_host to scope blast radius.

domains.domain: DISCOVERY / RECON - host, account, domain & trust enumeration via native Windows tooling

queries.use_case: Recon-binary activity per host
queries.query: source_type=windows_sysmon action=process_create command_line=/(whoami|nltest|systeminfo|ipconfig|tasklist|net view|net user|net group)/i | stats count by src_host, user | sort -count | head 30
queries.catches: Hosts/users running native discovery tooling (whoami/net/nltest/systeminfo) - first-stage recon after a foothold.

queries.use_case: AD account & group enumeration
queries.query: source_type=windows_sysmon action=process_create command_line=/net1?\s+(user|group|localgroup)/i | stats count by src_host, command_line | sort -count | head 30
queries.catches: net user/group/localgroup invocations - direct domain account & privileged-group enumeration.

queries.use_case: Recon tool diversity (staging signal)
queries.query: source_type=windows_sysmon action=process_create command_line=/(whoami|nltest|systeminfo|ipconfig|tasklist|net view|net user)/i | stats dc(process_name) as tools, count as runs by src_host | where runs > 5 | sort -runs | head 30
queries.catches: Hosts running many distinct recon binaries in a tight window - the rapid-enumeration burst of an operator orienting on a new box.

queries.use_case: Domain trust / DC enumeration via nltest
queries.query: source_type=windows_sysmon action=process_create command_line=/nltest.*(dclist|domain_trusts|dsgetdc)/i | table src_host,user,command_line | head 50
queries.catches: nltest /dclist /domain_trusts - mapping domain controllers & trusts ahead of lateral movement (rare-event detector).

queries.use_case: Per-host recon sweep (retro IR)
queries.query: source_type=windows_sysmon action=process_create command_line=/(whoami|nltest|systeminfo|ipconfig|tasklist|net |quser|arp -a)/i | stats count as recon_cmds, dc(process_name) as tools by src_host | where recon_cmds > 10 | sort -recon_cmds | head 30
queries.catches: Hosts with heavy multi-tool recon volume over 24h - scopes which machines an intruder enumerated from.
